title: Finite-level exchange is the restricted ambient exchange
statement:
Let $\Lambda,I,P_i=\Lambda/I^i$ ($i\geq1$), $K_i=K\otimes^L_\Lambda P_i$, and their transitions be the complete coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum]. Let $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$, and the automorphisms $\operatorname{Fr}_T$ ($T=X,Y,X',Y'$) form a Frobenius-equivariant datum [def-weil-pbc-frobenius-tower-datum], including its chosen Cartesian Frobenius faces. Use the ordinary derived operations on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with constant coefficient sheaves. For each $T$, let $\operatorname{Res}_{i,T}:D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},P_i)\to D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ be termwise restriction of scalars along $\Lambda_T\to(P_i)_T$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For every edge $u:U\to V$ among $f,f',g,g'$ and the Frobenius automorphisms, the canonical comparisons
$$\operatorname{Res}_{i,U}Lu^*_{P_i}\cong Lu^*_{\Lambda}\operatorname{Res}_{i,V},\qquad
\operatorname{Res}_{i,V}Ru_{*,P_i}\cong Ru_{*,\Lambda}\operatorname{Res}_{i,U}$$
are natural isomorphisms. Under them, restriction of scalars takes the derived pullback composition comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] to their $\Lambda$-linear versions, and takes the canonical exchange transformation for either Frobenius face [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] with coefficients $P_i$ to its $\Lambda$-linear version. In particular, the finite-level maps $\beta_{f,i}$ at $K_i$ and $\beta_{f',M_i}$ at $M_i\in D(X'_{\mathrm{proet}},P_i)$ in the datum, and the pullback comparisons $\kappa_g,\kappa_{g'}$, agree after restriction with the corresponding ambient transformations. Writing $\Phi_T=L\operatorname{Fr}_T^*$ and suppressing these endpoint comparisons, for $m,n\geq1$, every ambient morphism $u:K_m\to K_n$, and every ambient morphism $s:M_m\to M_n$, one has
$$Rf_*\Phi_X(u)\,\beta_{f,m}=\beta_{f,n}\,\Phi_Y(Rf_*u),\qquad
Rf'_*\Phi_{X'}(s)\,\beta_{f',M_m}=\beta_{f',M_n}\,\Phi_{Y'}(Rf'_*s).$$
Here ambient means a morphism in the indicated derived category with coefficients $\Lambda$, and the same ambient naturality applies to $\kappa_g,\kappa_{g'}$.
